A monogram is never the finished state — scripts/verify-images.mjs fails any slot claiming a photograph that paints none.

frame_comment: Machine-readable geometry, read by scripts/verify-frame.mjs. Every value is from the saved extract. These frames are NOT the People First Card — the header and subject are plain Figma frames, and the stage card is `Clickable card` from a non-People-First library (F-018) — so they are built in local CSS and asserted here rather than merely declared.  The stepper, the avatar, the chevron and every gap inside the card were built from the extract and then measured by nothing at all — named as `still open` twice before being closed. They were correct because they had been transcribed an hour earlier, which is exactly the standing the subject field's width had the day it turned out to be 10px wrong (F-024). Asserted now, from the verbatim `Clickable card` extract.

divergences.components: Stepper, People, Rectangle Tags and Right arrow come from a non-People-First library (F-018).
divergences.tags: Figma uses Rectangle Tags with alpha fills. The prototype uses the People First Tags component.
divergences.personName12px: 12px is not on the People First type ramp; the prototype uses the 13px label class with a declared `accept`.
divergences.buttonWeight: Figma draws Close case 13px Regular; .pf-button is 13px SemiBold. Case matches on this frame, so weight is the only difference.
